slides.title: Black Holes
slides.subtitle: Where gravity wins, light gives up, and physics gets weird.

slides.text: A black hole is not a hole. It is matter squeezed so tight that nothing can escape it.

slides.title: How they are born
slides.subtitle: Most black holes start as giant stars that run out of fuel.

slides.title: The death of a giant star

steps.label: Fuel
steps.text: A star 20x the Sun burns hydrogen for millions of years.

steps.label: Collapse
steps.text: Fuel runs out. Gravity crushes the core in under a second.

steps.label: Supernova
steps.text: The outer layers blast away in a blinding explosion.

steps.label: Singularity
steps.text: The core keeps shrinking into a point of infinite density.

slides.label: Solar masses in M87*
slides.note: The first black hole ever photographed, by the Event Horizon Telescope in 2019.

cards.title: Stellar
cards.text: 5 to 100 Suns. Left behind by collapsing massive stars.

cards.title: Intermediate
cards.text: Hundreds to thousands of Suns. Rare, and hard to find.

cards.title: Supermassive
cards.text: Millions to billions of Suns. One sits at the centre of most galaxies.

slides.title: What happens if you fall in
points: Time slows down for you, as seen from far away.
Tidal forces stretch you thin: spaghettification.
Past the event horizon, every path leads inward.
No signal you send can ever get back out.

right.title: Reality
points: From far away they pull like any other mass
We image their glowing disks and shadows

slides.title: The information paradox
slides.text: Hawking showed black holes slowly evaporate. If they vanish, what happens to the information about everything that fell in? Physicists are still arguing.

slides.title: The universe is stranger than we think
slides.subtitle: Thank you. Questions?
